A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

HHV-8 encodes a viral IL-6 that has the potential to contribute directly to pathogenesis and viral CCLs that have the potential to do the same, although their roles may be less direct than that of viral IL- 6.

HHV-8-encoded cytokines, like other viral factors, are multifunctional proteins that contribute to the virus' ability to evade the immune system, to establish latency and to promote the development of disease.

HHV-8-encoded cytokines have the potential for multiple functions in the pathogenesis of HHV-8-related malignancies and that the development of therapeutic approaches to target viral IL-6 is a promising approach to the treatment of these diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
viral IL-6 is a potent proinflammatory cytokine that can induce the expression of several chemokines in endothelial cells, including the viral CCL-3 and CCL-4 ligands.
viral IL-6 is an important factor in the pathogenesis of Kaposi's and Castleman's disease, and that the viral chemokine homologues may also be important in the development of Kaposi sarcoma.
the viral chemokine genes are not essential for HHV-8 replication and are dispensable for HHV-6 replication, suggesting that the viral chemokinogens are not required for HHV- 8 pathogenesis.
